To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the conformational equilibrium between folded and extended structures is the origin of elasticity in elastomeric proteins; (ii) the PPII structure is the most probable conformation in elastomeric protein; (iii) the presence of a glycine residue at every 3-4 residues is not necessary to obtain a PPII structure, but the presence of a PPII conformation is necessary to obtain elasticity.
elastomeric proteins show a conformational ensemble that is mainly constituted by beta-turns, polyproline II helices, and beta-strands.

the molecular mechanism of the elasticity of elastomery proteins is the same and is based on a dynamic equilibrium between folded (main beta-turns) structures and extended conformations (mainly PPII).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the structural basis of the elasticity of the elastomeric protein resilin by CD spectroscopy.
the study of the molecular mechanism underlying elasticity in elastomeric proteins.
the molecular mechanism that allows the elasticity of elastomery proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all elastomeric proteins, including resilin, share a common molecular mechanism of elasticity.
the molecular mechanism of elastin elasticity is a dynamic equilibrium between folded and extended conformations, and the PPII structure is the main conformation of the extended state.

the molecular mechanism of the elasticity of elastomers is due to the presence of a conformational ensemble constituted by PPII structure, beta-turns, beta-strands, and beta-sheet, and that CD spectroscopy represents an invaluable spectroscopic technique to analyze the conformation of elastomeric protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conformational equilibria of elastomeric sequences are characterized by the presence of PII and beta-turns, with the latter being the major contributors to elasticity.

the molecular mechanism of elastomeric protein elasticity is based on the equilibrium between folded and unfolded conformations, which is driven by the presence of glycine residues in their sequences.
the molecular basis for elasticity of elastomery proteins is the presence of a high content of PPII helix.
The main takeaway from our work is that

CD spectroscopy can provide important insights into the molecular mechanism underlying elasticity of elastomery proteins, and that this approach is applicable also for the analysis of new proteins with elastomeric properties.
the conformational ensemble of elastomeric protein can be described by a single conformational model, which is based on a dynamic equilibrium between folded and unfolded conformations.
the presence of PII structure in the unfolded state is not a peculiarity of the elastomeric domain of resilin.
